steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Atomic structure: p⁺, n⁰, e⁻; isotopes = same Z, different A; electron config: 1s^22s^22p⁶...

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ionisation energy: increases across period (↑Z_eff), decreases down group (↑shielding, ↑n)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Ionic: metal + non-metal, electron transfer, lattice; Covalent: non-metal + non-metal, sharing

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Electronegativity (Pauling): increases across, decreases down; >1.7 ionic, <0.4 non-polar covalent

steps.title: Worked example
steps.body: Q: Explain why H₂O has a higher boiling point than H₂S despite similar molecular mass --- Solution: H₂O has H-bonding (O is highly electronegative, lone pairs); H₂S has only dipole-dipole and London forces. H-bonding is much stronger -> more energy to separate molecules -> higher BP

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Write electron configuration of Fe^2⁺ (Z=26) | Predict shape and bond angle of NH₃, CO₂, SF₆ | Rank boiling points: CH₄, NH₃, H₂O, HF -- explain
